changeSet.comment: nexus.rdr229_restamp(p_table text) RETURNS text, the operator's way back from an orphan (RDR-229 P3.1 fix round A, critique S1 / code review F4). A stamp move whose on_complete found an orphan row (a name with no registry row in its tenant) COMPLETES and leaves the table's CHECK NOT VALID; it does not run again, so registering the missing collection stamped nothing and the VALIDATE kept raising 23514. SELECT nexus.rdr229_restamp('chunk_orphaned_at') registers the table's stamp move again: a new data_moves row (a label is the primary key) named rdr229-stamp-<table>-rerun-N that supersedes the previous move of the chain (the completed original, or the last re-run) and copies its template, verification, on_complete, throttle and changeset_id, so the worker stamps the rows that have become resolvable and validates the CHECK(s). It registers only when the chain's last move is complete, a CHECK of the table is NOT VALID and no orphan row remains (an orphan being a row that names a collection no registry row of its tenant carries); otherwise it says why, as text, and raises nothing and writes nothing. The list of tables, name columns, id columns and constraints is a copy of db/rdr229/p31-checks.tsv (the one list), pinned equal by Rdr229RestampFunctionIntegrationTest. SECURITY INVOKER and EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC: nexus.data_moves is the migrating role's, nexus_svc holds no grant on it. It reads the registry and the table to look for an orphan and writes one row to nexus.data_moves; no row of a user-data table changes. THE BOUND (confirmation review N3). The probe is a scan of the table with no index to help (a name set, no id, no registry row): on chunks, about 13 s on gp3 by the P3.2 arithmetic, and it runs under an operator's call that has no statement_timeout of its own. A SET (LOCAL or the function's own SET clause) of statement_timeout inside the function does NOT bound it: PostgreSQL arms that timer when the top-level statement starts, and a plpgsql function is one statement (measured on the PG17 test image: pg_sleep(2) under a 200 ms setting ran 2 s in all three forms). So the probe reads the table in block ranges (ctid ranges, one TID range scan per range and per partition) and checks the clock between ranges: it stops once nexus.rdr229_restamp_probe_ms has passed (default 60000, 60 s, about four times chunks' measured full scan). On timeout the operator sees the text 'not registered: the orphan probe of <table> did not finish within N ms (K of M blocks read); nothing was registered', which names the setting; nothing was written, so the same call can be run again, with a longer bound for the session if the table needs it (SET nexus.rdr229_restamp_probe_ms = 300000). nexus.rdr229_restamp_probe_blocks (default 8192, 64 MB) is the range size; a test sets it to 1. DATA EFFECT: none at boot; the function is created, not called. The rollback drops it.
